_comment: One source of truth for week 9's rubric. The grader scores from this file, the homework's grading table is copied from it, and you can read it. `suite` says which test run scores an item — 'checks' is `dotnet test Project.Checks` (canonical, replaced wholesale by the grader), 'tests' is `dotnet test Project.Tests` (the student's OWN suite, run as-is and never replaced). The items are in TASK order: Task 1 is check 1 plus the student's own fact, and Tasks 2, 3 and 4 are checks 2, 3 and 4 — the homework mirrors the lab task for task. The dictated student fact carries the WEEK rather than a check number, per week 8's change. Check 4 (Sorted) is the heaviest item in the week on purpose: it is the only one that catches a Sorted() which reorders the registry in place, and that is the week's central trap. Check 1 stays at 2 like every came-forward check even though it is the safety net for the Task 1 rewrite of Find and Load. The graded repo is the PROJECT repo (D1b).

Check1_WeeksFourToEightStillHold.label: Weeks 4-8 still hold — Topic, no public fields, All() copies, Find and Remove behave (including the empty-handed answer), IListed kept by record and registry, Everything() intact, Add refuses a duplicate, and Save/Load still round-trip

Week9_FindComesBackEmptyHanded.label: Your test: Find hands back the record it holds, and null for a name nobody has — written by you, green in your own suite

Check2_TheRegistryFindsEveryMatch.label: Matching(term) hands back every record whose name contains the term, in order, and an empty list when none do

Check3_TheRegistryHandsBackItsNames.label: Names() hands back one name per record, in the order they were added

Check4_TheRegistryComesBackInOrder.label: Sorted() hands back every record in order by name — and leaves the registry's own order alone

repoReachable.label: Public project repo exists at the URL you submitted, and clones

programRuns.label: The program builds and runs without crashing — even when fed nothing but Enter

gitignoreClean.label: bin/ and obj/ tracked nowhere in the project repo — the .gitignore holding

commits.label: 3+ commits on THIS week's branch 👀 (meaningful messages are a judgment call)

mergedPr.label: A merge commit on main — this week's branch → pull request → merge
